findings.text: Thread state reset for reuse clears per thread TLS descriptors and restores floating point and protection key defaults for the current task, building on separate FPU and breakpoint helpers.

Timestamp counter access is gated per thread by a flag that stays coherent with a processor control bit. Query reports enabled versus faulting mode and update selects between those two modes with rejection of other values.

User CPUID faulting is gated per thread by a flag that stays coherent with vendor specific control storage, using a per CPU shadow on one vendor and a hardware configuration bit on another. Mode query and update are only available when the faulting capability is present.

New execution startup reenables previously suppressed CPUID faulting, conditionally drops speculative store bypass suppression across the boundary when noexec semantics apply with a control refresh, and resets address untagging for the new image.

IO permission bitmap handling invalidates prior state on switch away and lazily enables state for the incoming thread. Copy occurs only when sequence identity changes with coverage of the larger prior extent, supports an emulation mode that permits all ports, and refreshes the TSS limit against virtualization truncation.

Speculative store bypass coordination uses a small record holding a shared peer link with a raw spinlock plus a disable request field and a local state field, instantiated per CPU with a zero index constant for the local slot.

Extended context switch reconciles IO bitmap with user return notification plus single step debug control and timestamp with CPUID gating differences and speculative control state, forcing a full control refresh when a forced update marker is present on either side.
Processor control toggling keeps a per CPU cached copy and only writes hardware when the toggled value differs, preserving interrupt disabled context.

Idle entry verifies timestamp adjust state and touches watchdog state. The main idle dispatcher invokes the installed idle routine and the dead CPU path never returns. The monitor wait variant avoids sleep when rescheduling is pending while clearing polling on exit.

Timestamp adjust verification is skipped without the adjust capability and when the clock is already unstable or within a rate limit window. Otherwise it restores a per CPU expected value on mismatch and warns once with additional warning on resume.

Post ACPI initialization checks for an AMD idle erratum via a pending message mask. When affected it records the bug and marks the timestamp clock unstable without nonstop capability, enables tick broadcast need, and logs the workaround.
Boot idle selection uses IDLE_NO_OVERRIDE as default with IDLE_POLL and IDLE_HALT and IDLE_NOMWAIT selected by poll and halt and nomwait boot strings.

Stack alignment applies bounded downward randomization unless disabled by personality or global switch and then aligns to a sixteen byte boundary. Heap start randomization uses a smaller extent for thirty two bit address mode and a larger extent otherwise.
Wait channel reporting acquires the target stack and walks unwind frames past scheduler addresses. It returns the first non scheduler return address or zero when unavailable.

Return address recovery yields zero once unwinding is complete. Frame and table based variants additionally filter by kernel text membership while the guess variant dereferences the current stack slot with recovery processing.

Segment base control provides per task FS and GS setters and getters with user range validation plus selector clearing and distinct current versus remote CPU paths. It uses fast per thread storage when modern base instructions exist with fallback through TLS descriptors or LDT entries otherwise.

Thread flag and CPU control coherence is protected by disabling preemption across the paired update. Inactive GS base access is protected by saving and restoring interrupt state, LDT inspection holds the address space context lock, and tagged address enabling holds the address space write lock.

Sixty four bit control also supports mapping a VDSO image at a chosen address reporting its size. It enables linear address masking only for the current address space when single threaded and compatible with accelerator bindings, installing a control mask and untag mask with remote CPU propagation and a persistent lock.

Shadow stack control distinguishes status query with feature locking plus checkpoint restore unlocking for remote tasks and current only enable or disable. Locked features are refused and only one feature may change per call, with write protection and shadow stack subfeatures using separate handlers.

Shadow stack enabling is idempotent when already active and requires hardware support with sixty four bit context. It allocates a sized region and programs supervisor and user protection MSRs under FPU protection, recording base with size and feature enablement.

Missing IO bitmap state triggers a one time warning with flag clearing and invalidation. Remote only base writers warn on current use, and invalid mode values with unsupported capabilities plus wrong address space targets and busy multithreaded LAM attempts and malformed idle strings are reported as errors.

Architecture control options include ARCH_GET_CPUID with ARCH_SET_CPUID and extended state queries ARCH_GET_XCOMP_SUPP with ARCH_GET_XCOMP_PERM with ARCH_REQ_XCOMP_PERM plus guest variants, segment operations ARCH_SET_GS with ARCH_SET_FS with ARCH_GET_FS with ARCH_GET_GS, VDSO mapping variants, tagged address operations with LAM_U57_BITS extent, and shadow stack operations ARCH_SHSTK_ENABLE with ARCH_SHSTK_DISABLE with ARCH_SHSTK_LOCK with ARCH_SHSTK_UNLOCK with ARCH_SHSTK_STATUS.
Shared coordination state includes a stop mask for CPUs with a boot selected idle override and a per CPU shadow of miscellaneous feature enables used to preserve CPUID faulting intent.
Speculative bypass state carries its own raw spinlock for shared access. Shadow stack MSR programming is serialized by holding FPU state loaded across the update.
Xen default idle installation records whether an override was already present and installs the default idle routine, reporting the prior state to the caller.

The offline CPU dead path never returns via a terminal fault. The inactive GS base update avoids base instructions under virtualized or alternate entry modes in favor of MSR access with instrumentation bracketing, and monitor wait flushes the watched flag location on affected hardware.

Timestamp and CPUID gating use PR_TSC_SIGSEGV with PR_TSC_ENABLE and TIF_NOTSC with TIF_NOCPUID correlated with X86_CR4_TSD and fault control bits MSR_MISC_FEATURES_ENABLES_CPUID_FAULT with MSR_K7_HWCR_CPUID_USER_DIS_BIT, while debug stepping uses DEBUGCTLMSR_BTF and idle uses MSR_K8_INT_PENDING_MSG with K8_INTP_C1E_ACTIVE_MASK.

IO bitmap enablement distinguishes IO_BITMAP_OFFSET_VALID_ALL for full emulation from IO_BITMAP_OFFSET_VALID_MAP for mapped state. Timestamp adjust uses MSR_IA32_TSC_ADJUST and debug uses MSR_IA32_DEBUGCTLMSR, while shadow stack uses MSR_IA32_PL3_SSP with MSR_IA32_U_CET and CET_SHSTK_EN.

Task switch IO bookkeeping keeps bitmap storage with a prior maximum extent plus a prior sequence value and a base offset in the task state. Updates compare incoming maximum with sequence against stored values to size the copy and refresh enablement.

Thread execution state keeps FS base with GS base plus selector indices and a TLS descriptor array, an IO bitmap pointer with an emulation level, feature flags with a lock mask, and shadow stack base with size.
Address space tagging state keeps an untag mask with a LAM control mask and flag bits for forced tagged accelerator use plus a persistent LAM lock.
